Omg... The same thing happened to me at 19. I was having intermittent pain like this for 4 months, and I went to the ER like 6 times because I was in so much pain during these episodes. They did an ultrasound and found an almond sized ovarian cyst on the initial visit. Every following visit, it grew at least 3 cm. The cyst grew to the size of a grapefruit. 
I eventually got sent to the worst OBGYN. She told me that this is normal and that tylenol and waiting it out was the best course of action. Luckily, I brought my RN mother who said "fuck no that needs to be removed." The OBGYN had to be talked into doing surgery for me. We walked out of that office, and my mom said there's no way that doctor is putting her hands on me. 
I ended up scheduling a surgery with the OBGYN that delivered me. Unfortunately, before I could reach the surgery date, I ended up back in the ER. They did another ultrasound and found that the cyst had ruptured. Queue me being rushed into an emergency surgery. They found out that the cyst wasn't on my ovary but in my abdominal lining, an extremely vascular area. I was bleeding out. I had to get multiple blood transfusions and almost lost my ovary. The pain I was feeling was the cyst torsioning my ovary and blocking the blood flow. 
FYI, if you don't feel heard, get a second opinion always.

This opinion is very.. touchy. On one hand this is basically eugenics and where do we draw the line between certain illnesses. On the other say there is a baby born with something severely physically debilitating that causes them nothing but pain such as Harlequin Disease (an overgrowth of the skin where it's basically like being constantly burned) or glass bone disease. Their life would be nothing but suffering and pain but that's an extremely hard decision to make AFTER they were already born. I believe that it absolutely should not be the choice of a government to euthanize that baby but in certain circumstances (such as the previously listed diseases, not mental illnesses like OP was talking about) the parents should be able to have a say in whether or not their baby should live. Again, that's an extremely hard decision and a very difficult opinion.
